It was Little League baseball season, we're talking T-ball. It was tournament time for the Pirates. Our team color was purple and the only uniform we got back then was a T-shirt. It was a very badly managed tournament so there was like, hours for us to wait in-between games. At least it seemed like that to a kid. Also I remember it being very, very, very hot. The adults grabbed some shade while us kids occupied ourselves until the next game. In the area we were waiting in was a broken glass bottle, being dumb, daredevils some were running back and forth jumping over it. I soon joined in. Some of the older, bigger kids on team noticed what we were doing and posted themselves just before the bottle trying to give us a shove just before we jumped.

 

Yeah, we WERE that stupid.

 

It was great fun, run, duck under the shove, jump, laugh at the antagonizer, repeat. One of the bigger kids took a special interest in making sure I was the one to get shoved into the bottle. I took note and sat by the Adult in the area, an Assistant coach sitting under one of the trees. My Father was also an Assistant coach but I can't remember what he was doing at the time [on a water run?]. Well the bigger kid would wonder off, I'd get up, jump the bottle a few times, antagonize HIM now, then run back to the safe zone.

 

The adult, not sure why, gets frustrated, stands up and walks off or told the kid to do what he wanted, I don't remember. I do remember the kid then, to my horror, grabbing me by the wrist and start jerking me towards the bottle. I kicked and screamed, he got help from some of our teammates! To the bottle we all go, they throw me on top of it, I land in a push-up position over it, the broken glass just under my knee. Someone jumps on the back of my knees driving one into the glass.

 

I remember the crowd clearing, I turn over, the Head coach is there, I just randomly point to one kid screaming through tears that he did it. Not sure if he was even in on it to be honest. My Dad comes over asks what happened the Adult just says I was jumping over broken bottles. I screamed he was lying. The entire team backs the coach saying he was telling the truth. The star of the team lil Mackie Jills [name changed of course] offers the sage advice that I should get a beating for calling an adult a liar. Not only was this kid involved in throwing me onto broken glass, he was trying to get my ass whooped after! On the way to the hospital I keep crying how they lied, my Farther asks how the entire team was lying and I was the only one telling the truth? I would then repeat myself. He eventually told me to just be quiet about it. After the hospital my Father took me BACK to the ball field where the next game was in progress. I had to go up to bat, hit the ball and limp to first base in front of everyone.

 

I never thought of vengeance. All that access to bats, all those ripe melons sitting on the bench, the thought never crossed my mind until now... almost 40 years later!

 

Now I've lived a plentiful life, I've had a lot of worse and better times, why is THIS memory haunting me day and night now? PTSD? Kind of delayed, huh?

Well, it was game day again....sort of.

It was scoreless for most of the game, which was customary for Alabama prior to Kiffin's arrival. Like the last two years of Kiffin's tenure here, we are breaking in a new QB, we just don't know who it will be yet. QB play is usually the reason we tune into Bama spring games recently, but we don't expect much in April.

Good thing, too. We have so much work to do, I'm somewhat worried about what we'll see when we open with a retooled USC in September. We threw into double and even triple coverage all game, and we missed lots of open guys. In fact, the youngest guy out there, Jalen Hurts, was one of the more effective QBs for most of the first half, and he threw a TD late in the 4th. Blake Barnett created a nice drive in the 4th but that led to no points.

*Observations*

The defense looked really good. I'm not just saying that because it was scoreless for so long. Recent scrimmages saw Bo Scarborough run for 130+ yards on a staggering few number of rushes, and he didn't do that well today. That could be because of conservative play calling (everyone is watching), but I won't make excuses for him. He needs to keep his YPR up, but that defense....damn. Think about this: Jonathan Allen, the most experienced and monstrous DE we have, who skipped the draft to come back for his senior year, wasn't even playing.

Adam Griffith wasn't good at all. The loss of Piniero to Florida hurts, bad. After Griffith, there isn't anybody to pick up the tee, so he better not get injured or we go from questionable to undoubtedly terrible at the kicking position.

*Differences from last year*

Coker is gone, so QB is obviously the most important position to lock down. I'm confident that Saban will pull it off, especially with the mobility of our QBs. Even Cornwell can run when he has to, and the other guys were all recruited as dual-threat QBs.

Most of the D-line is gone, but Allen is back and Tim Williams....my god, that guy is going pro next year, no doubt, and he will be the next Von Miller. Speaking of Millers, Christian Miller wasn't too bad either, and I'm happy that he's doing well for as long as he's waited.

I worry about Rueben Foster running the defense. He's a senior, which surprised me because I thought we redshirted him, but oh well. He just didn't look in control, so the D-line is basically running on autopilot (or under Allen's leadership). This may be a year that we don't need a leader at MLB. Landon Collins was the leader of the secondary in 2013 and 2014, while Trey DePriest handled the Front 7. I could see that happening this year, with senior safety Eddie Jackson leading the secondary and senior DE Jonathan Allen handling the D-line. Then the linebackers will only have to focus on doing their jobs. After all, we have 7 returning starters on defense.

Calvin Ridley is there, and he made some great catches, but he dropped a wide open pass at one point, and so did a few other receivers. Saban seemed surprised by this, so I guess we'll have to work out kinks and nerves in bigger games this year.

Tight end play was evident. I saw a lot of passes to Miller Forristal on the second team, and OJ Howard got a few important looks. It seems like Kiffin wants to use his TEs in a way that we haven't since..well, ever....maybe Colin Peek, idk. Alabama hasn't had a go-to Kellen Winslow Jr. type guy TE I can remember, Saban prefers dual-purposes TEs that can block 80% of the time (hence our run-first, pass-block attack) and catch 100% of throws 20% throws....20% of the time, it works every time....that doesn't make any sense.

*Pros/Cons*

Pros are easily on defense, specifically the pass rush, which will disrupt QBs all season. Alabama may set sack records, but Saban doesn't care about sacks, he cares about "affecting the QB," and we'll do that fine. Another pro is Damien Harris, who ran better against the 2nd team defense than Bo did vs the 1st team defense. Since our defense is so deep, I give a lot of credit to Harris and the 2nd team O-line.

Cons are special teams (as usual), no clear starting QB (as usual, at least recently), and question on defensive leadership. Honestly, we can deal with the first two, but if that last one persists I see Alabama losing to high-powered and elaborate offenses like Tennessee, Auburn, and Texas A&M....haha, who am I kidding, we're not going to lose to those last two.

*Prediction*

Alabama will be really good again, but I worry about chemistry and the ability to stop spread offenses if we can't get our leadership together. Still, we're fast up front and very flexible. If we can get a clear leader(s) on defense, I see another SEC West title. If not, we might lose to one of the western Tigers, which are always close games, and I do NOT expect our game at Tennessee to go well. We've beat them 9 times in a row. It's hard to imagine a 10th, but they're in the SEC East, so we could feasibly lose to them in the regular season, run the table in the West, and play them again in the SEC Championship.

All said and done, I think Alabama goes 10-2 or 11-1 in the regular season, and depending on who we lose to, we could go the SEC Championship, where I give us a 50%+ chance to win no matter who we play.
